structured_plan.G: After both trees complete, select only candidates that pass the full public contract and compare their measured wall-clock results under the official protocol. Integrate the best candidate, test any combination rather than assuming gains are additive, then independently confirm final G on the separate confirmation seeds. Keep changes within src/candidate.cpp; preserve the API, thread budget, and exact earliest-index tie behavior.
structured_plan.analysis: Choose N=2: the valid baseline is a serial O(n) scan with a strict-less-than update, and its measured mean is 8.91365 μs (score 0.5). The available evidence does not break down timings by size, so treat it as one baseline measurement, not a per-size diagnosis. The timed sizes are 4093 and 65536 with a one-thread budget; parallelism is therefore not a useful distinct track. Two complementary scan optimizations merit research: explicit SIMD reduction and compiler-friendly scalar unrolling. Both must scan all elements for arbitrary inputs and return the first minimum for every valid size, including ties and extreme int32 values. Do not specialize to benchmark inputs.

children.objective: Explore an explicitly vectorized argmin scan using x86 SIMD intrinsics where supported by the build target. Reduce values and recover the smallest matching index correctly; handle tails and all valid n. Compare viable vector widths or reduction strategies using the official correctness and timing protocol. Do not rely on test-value assumptions or exceed the one-thread budget.
children.subject: Explicit SIMD argmin reduction

children.objective: Explore a scalar-only, compiler-friendly scan redesign, such as independent unrolled partial minima followed by an index-stable merge, without explicit x86 intrinsics or parallel execution. Preserve exact signed comparisons and smallest-index tie behavior for all valid inputs. Measure against the baseline at both timed sizes and retain only correctness-validated improvements.
children.subject: Scalar multi-accumulator scan
